The SNB manifesto

We're stuck, not broken.

A few things I believe.

Welcome. This is a catalog of the ideas, the signals, that drive our work. I'm Justin, a therapist, best known for teaching Polyvagal Theory in plain English: the Stuck Not Broken podcast, three books, the Unstucking Academy, and the Stuck Not Broken app. Below is what we stand for, and what I won't do. Open any one to read the why, or wander the numbered list in any order. Take your time.

We're not broken. We're stuck.

Stuck is a state of our nervous system, not a character flaw and not a broken part. States are temporary by nature, which means they can be worked with. That one reframe, from broken to stuck, is the whole point of Stuck Not Broken. It changes what we do next.

Our bodies are protecting us, even now.

Our nervous systems aren't malfunctioning. Whatever they're doing right now, they learned to do to keep us safe, and they're still trying. That's an old and smart response doing its job, even when it's inconvenient. Understanding that comes before any technique.

Stuck is possibility.

This isn't a promise about when. It's the simple fact that a state is a state, not a sentence. States shift, and we get to be part of how they shift. The hope lives in the biology, not in a countdown.

Biology, not willpower.

This was never about trying harder or wanting it more. We work with the body, in small repeatable reps, the way we'd build any kind of capacity. Gritting our teeth tends to make a defensive state louder, not quieter.

Plain English, not clinical labels.

We're not a "disorder," and we're not a diagnosis code. Plain words we can actually use in the moment matter more here. The clinical terms have their place, but they're not how we talk to ourselves at 2am.

No state is a flaw.

Safety, fight-or-flight, and shutdown are states our bodies move through, not verdicts about who we are. Each one made sense at some point. The x in our mark just names shutdown. It never meant broken.

We're not meant to do this alone.

Regulation isn't a solo project, and needing other people isn't a weakness. Nervous systems settle in the presence of other steady ones, which is why community and live practice matter here. We're wired to co-regulate. That's the design, not a bug.

Practice, not protocol.

No reset in seven days, no vagus-nerve trick, no gadget, no hack, and I'll never sell you one. Skills we keep, built slowly, beat a shortcut that doesn't hold. (The science is real. The hacks built on top of it are what I'm against.)

I won't rush you.

No countdowns, no "doors closing," no fake deadlines, no manufactured urgency. I'd rather lose the sale than scare you into it. A nervous system that's been pressured doesn't learn safety, so pressure would defeat the whole point.

What you tell it stays yours.

I won't sell your data, and you can delete all of it in one tap. No email to support, no dark-pattern maze. What you share stays yours. A felt sense of safety is the whole product, and surveillance would break it.

I'd rather you graduate than stay.

The academy exists so you won't need the academy. If the work is working, you need it less over time, and that's the goal, not a leak in the funnel. I'm not building a place for you to get stuck in.

I'll be straight about what this does.

This won't make a hard feeling vanish, and I won't pretend it will. The goal is to move through it faster, and to be less afraid of it when it comes. Honest scope is a feature. I'd rather under-promise and have it hold.

Peer, not guru.

I get dysregulated too, and I'll tell you when I don't know something. A steady voice across the table, not a stage and not a guru. You're allowed to disagree with me and stay.

If you don't know where you are right now, you can start at stucknotbroken.com/stuck . Or just watch a video. No card, no wall.

We're allowed to do nothing today.

Some days the move is to rest and come back tomorrow. That counts as practice too. There's no streak to keep and no one grading us. Take your time.

Justin

Stuck Not Broken
Justin Sunseri, LMFT
